description:
FILED s454ac (round 12 perf agent) while closing #680.

#680 removed the per-iteration re-parse from the m// family: p-regex /
p-regex-from-parts are memoized on source text, the compiled scanner lives
in the p-regex-match struct (%compiled), and cl-ppcre:scan is a direct
funcall.  The s/// family has the SAME disease, untouched:

    my $n = 0;  $n++ while $x =~ s/a/b/;
    -> (p-while (p-=~ $x (p-subst "a" "b")) (p-post++ $n))

(p-subst "a" "b") runs make-p-subst-op per ITERATION, and do-regex-subst
then runs perl-regex-to-ppcre on the pattern (eight regex-replace-all
passes -- 51% of the m//g loop before #680) plus %pcl-create-scanner with
its FORMAT-built key, per execution.  tr/// via p-tr has the analogous
shape (expand-tr-chars per execution -- measure before assuming).

THE FIX SHAPE, copied from #680 (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only):
  1. Memoize p-subst on (pattern replacement modifiers) -- BUT the
     replacement can be a FUNCTION (s///e and interpolated replacements
     compile to a lambda); a lambda is a fresh object per call site
     evaluation, so either key the memo only when the replacement is a
     STRING, or cache the compiled scanner separately from the op (see 2).
     A p-subst-op is mutated nowhere (grep first, as #680 did for
     p-regex-match).
  2. Give p-subst-op a %compiled slot filled once (pattern conversion +
     scanner + reg-names + closers + the modifier member tests) -- this
     alone removes the re-parse even where the op struct itself cannot be
     shared.
  3. do-regex-subst's non-e branch scans the subject up to THREE times
     (scan for match vars, regex-replace(-all), all-matches-as-strings for
     the count) -- the count and the match vars can come from one pass.
  4. Route its cl-ppcre:scan / regex-replace calls through %p-ppcre-scan or
     hoist the simple-string coercion the same way (a str-buffer subject is
     copied whole per call by ppcre's maybe-coerce-to-simple-string).

MEASURE FIRST (the #680 recipe): sb-sprof on
  my $x = "a" x 50000; my $n = 0; $n++ while $x =~ s/a/b/;
and an s///g one-shot on a large subject; ladder before/after.  Bar:
targeted regex Pl/t files green (match-vars-01, regexp-subst-01,
regex-gpos-01), probes vs perl for s///e capture state and s///r, and the
full sweep at the next merge (cl/ change, invisible to corpus-diff).


=== DONE (s474, Fable, 2026-09-06) === Shipped as #1250 (a regex/subst/tr LITERAL builds its op once per SITE, `%p-op-once`) + #1251 (the s/// op carries its COMPILED record, `%p-subst-compiled`) in perf round 29 (s470bu, main 8a879a57): subste -43.5 % isolated, json-rt +99 % vs main, regexg +32 %, textproc +30 %.  This task described exactly that residue; closed by pointer.
subject: Target-A residue of #680: the s/// family re-parses per execution -- (p-subst "a" "b") is built per loop iteration and do-regex-subst re-runs perl-regex-to-ppcre + the scanner format key per call; give it the #680 memo treatment
